video_title: Should the Lakers Pursue Jonathan Kuminga? - ESPN's Brian Windhorst on Sedano and Kap

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Lakers' roster overhaul and player health
quotes.excerpt: It's a full-on makeover. For a team that made the second round, that's really unheard of.
quotes.quote: First off, a fascinating stat from our guy Stats Williams was that obviously there's an asterisk because Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves were hurt. But the top five minutes played guys from the Lakers' playoffs are not back. For a team that made the second round, that's really unheard of. It's a full-on makeover. That's number one.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the value of the Mo Bamba contract
quotes.excerpt: I like the value that they got Mo Bamba on. A lot of people in the league like that.
quotes.quote: I like the value that they got Mo Bamba on. A lot of people in the league I've talked to like that contract and like that value as a Rui Hachimura replacement. Now, the thing about it is, Rui signed for $14 million with the Clippers. I'm not sure he would have signed for $14 million with the Lakers. He signed for $14 million after his market got set. This is the same situation with like Tobias Harris. Tobias Harris signed for $16 million with the Spurs. I'm not sure he would have stayed in Detroit for $16 million. Sometimes players will switch teams and take less money as opposed to stay and take less money.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst's critique of the Lakers' defensive personnel changes
quotes.excerpt: I'm not in love with the other moves because I think Grant Williams does not have positional size.
quotes.quote: I'm not in love with the other moves because I think Grant Williams does not have positional size. And while he will be better offensively, I think he will be a step down defensively from Marcus Smart. Sexton is a bulldog, that's his nickname, and I think fans will love how hard he plays. Everywhere he's ever played, all the way back to Alabama, have loved the way he plays. Young Bull I think is his nickname, actually, not Bulldog. But he doesn't have positional size and I don't think he's as good of a shooter as Kennard. So defensively, which is what you need on the perimeter, I'm not sure they got better there.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the potential of the Luka, Reeves, and Kessler trio
quotes.excerpt: Luka, Reeves, and Kessler, like that is a real trio. That trio is going to win a lot.
quotes.quote: That said, Luka, Reeves, and Kessler, like that is a real trio. That trio is going to win a lot of games. You're going to see good chemistry there. That is really something to build off of, but I'm not in love with the rest of the build out. I could be proven wrong, but I'm not super excited about it based on who walked out the door.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the market reality for Jonathan Kuminga
quotes.excerpt: Two teams in the last year have moved on from him. You did not see any team.
quotes.quote: I just want to point out about Kuminga, the reason you like Kuminga is you give him a big role and you hope he can produce. But I just want to point out that two teams in the last year have moved on from him. And you did not see any team go commit any significant resources to get him. That does not mean he will not have a great year. I will just say to you, you just have to acknowledge and understand that there is a reason why he would be available for relative cheap.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the financial incentives for acquiring Jonathan Kuminga
quotes.excerpt: You feel better having Kuminga at a couple million a year as opposed to having him at 25.
quotes.quote: You feel better having Kuminga at a couple million a year as opposed to having him at 25 million a year. So that's one thing that changes everything. That colors the way you're going to evaluate him, absolutely. But look, the getting excited about Jonathan Kuminga has been an annual right now for like five years. So that does not mean that he won't have a great year. I'm just telling you, for five years I've listened to how Jonathan Kuminga is going to have a breakout season. And so I am just going to wait back and watch.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Lakers' Andre Drummond acquisition comparison
quotes.excerpt: When the Lakers signed Andre Drummond, compared it to acquiring Dennis Rodman.
quotes.quote: When the Lakers signed Andre Drummond, compared it to acquiring Dennis Rodman. And I said, you know he has been released in the middle of the season for a reason. So there are examples in NBA history of players who were left by the side of the road who come to a new team, get a new situation, and thrive. And that's what the Lakers would hope there. But you have to be responsible when you have your expectations about the player you're getting.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the Lakers' salary cap strategy with Reeves and Luka
quotes.excerpt: I don't think it's a very good idea to have 70% of your salary cap taken up by two.
quotes.quote: Regardless of what you think about Brad Stevens' decision to trade Jaylen Brown, Brad Stevens has demonstrated to be very good at his job. And he said, I don't think it's a very good idea to have 70% of your salary cap taken up by two players who do very similar things. And that's essentially what the Lakers have with Reeves and Luka. They're slightly different, but they're the same type of player. And so to overcome that, you have to be very efficient on other parts of your roster. And if you can get Kuminga at a couple million dollars a year and he plays that role very well, that's what the Lakers can do.
